title: I built a roguelike where every single card is generated by AI - the game literally invents new cards as you play
author: GangstaRob7

comments.author: GangstaRob7
comments.body:
Hello! This is my project I have been working on for a while now - the aim is to turn generative AI into a fun game where you can craft endless cards, and battle against an onslaught of cards other players have crafted. I hope you enjoy!

Game Webpage - [https://infinite-card.net/](https://infinite-card.net/)  
Reddit Community - [https://www.reddit.com/r/InfiniteCard/](https://www.reddit.com/r/InfiniteCard/)

comments.author: JustJacque
comments.body: Does it actually have any meaningful gameplay or choice? The video makes it look like a no.

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body: Well I suppose you would have to play it and you can determine that for yourself. I will say there is certainly some skill involved, as you must manage your resources (cards and powerups) to make sure you can beat each incoming enemy.

replies.author: PixelSteel
replies.body: What about infinite craft? What meaningful gameplay does it have? It’s practically the same premise except with words instead of cards.

comments.author: final_boss_editing
comments.body: Reminds me of infinite craft. Would love to learn how you set this up!

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body: Sure, what would you like to know? It uses Google's Gemini for the text-based effects

comments.author: Mr-Bovine_Joni
comments.body: This is really cool. I assume you use an online API to an LLM to generate output? Does it generate the images for you as well? What types of guardrails did you have to build into the prompt?

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body: Yep that's right! I didn't really build guardrails in the prompt, but I have guardrails after the response. So my code vets each AI response in various ways after

comments.author: Ordinary_Issue_3003
comments.body: Interesting! Do we discover images or words (which one is unique)? And most interestingly, how do you decide the winners in a deathmatch?

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body: Hey! The card for all intensive purposes is defined by the name. Although, the images are unique as well and is tied to that name. To resolve the battles, it just sends a message to Gemini, asking it to evaluate which wins the battle, and Gemini needs to explain its reasoning. So if you disagree with the outcome, you can at least see where the AI was coming from.

comments.author: qqepyepuep
comments.body:
It looks fun!
What are the battle rules? Eg, taylor swift vs cloud?

replies.author: GangstaRob7
replies.body:
It asks an LLM to determine who would win in a battle between the two and explain its reasoning. This is extremely open ended, and the LLM will latch on to different qualities of both cards, but more often than not, it is able to determine what a human would intuitively say would win.

For your example, the AI might say, "Taylor Swift is an iconic figure, and is thus unaffected by a mere cloud, which is made of Water Vapor and wouldn't be able to harm her. With her impressive stage presence, she slices through the cloud with her catchy lyrics."
